round: Adversarial re-review of the release-prep fixes, 2026-10-14
method: Independent re-checks, not a restatement: git ls-files/stat for modes, ast.parse with feature_version=(3, 11) and (3, 9) for CI compatibility, curl for URL reachability, cffconvert 2.0.0 in an isolated venv for citation validity, GitHub docs and the Linguist overrides document for config semantics, and the actions/python-versions manifest for CI platform availability.

findings.title: Citation repository URL is not reachable
findings.why_it_matters: The release-prep commit promoted this URL from `url:` to `repository-code:`. CFF schema validation and cffconvert both accept the file regardless, so nothing in the toolchain catches a dead citation URL.
findings.disposition: Resolved: the maintainer supplied https://github.com/e-mudao/rnd-workflow-team-skills, which returns HTTP 200 and whose API metadata identifies this project (public, default branch main). Writing that URL also exposed that the earlier identity ('emudao', from local git config) was a different GitHub account, so the citation identity was aligned to 'e-mudao'.

findings.title: No git remote is configured
findings.why_it_matters: The earlier report called the first Actions run 'the only remaining boundary'; in fact nothing has been pushed, so the P1 workflow fix has never executed anywhere.
findings.disposition: Fixed as reporting: boundaries corrected in summary.json and stated under CHANGELOG Notes.

findings.title: .gitattributes fix did not fix behaviour
findings.evidence: Linguist supports only linguist-detectable, -documentation, -generated, -language and -vendored; a bare `linguist` attribute is not among them, so `-linguist` remained a no-op after the spelling fix, while the commit message claimed the no-op attributes were fixed.
findings.disposition: Fixed: `-linguist-detectable` on all three patterns, with a comment naming the documented attribute.

findings.title: CHANGELOG overstated the citation identity
findings.evidence: cffconvert renders `author = {emudao}`; the filed identity is the repository's configured git handle placed in family-names, not a verified personal name.
findings.disposition: Fixed: reworded to 'the maintainer identity configured in this repository (emudao)', and the cffconvert result is now cited.

findings.title: Evidence tooling was 0600 on disk
findings.evidence: stat showed -rw------- for evidence/release-fixes-2026-10-14/validate_release_config.py and evidence/final-review-2026-10-14/reprod.py, against a repository convention of 0644. Git records 100644 for both, so a clone is unaffected, but a tarball of the working tree would not be.
findings.disposition: Fixed: chmod 644 on both. Root cause is that agent-written files default to 0600.

findings.title: CI never exercised the Python floor the checker claims
findings.evidence: The workflow ran only 3.11 while the checker claims 3.9+; Path.is_relative_to is itself a 3.9 API. All 16 .py files parse at feature_version=(3, 9) and use no 3.12+ API.
findings.disposition: Fixed: matrix 3.9/3.11/3.13, after confirming in the actions/python-versions manifest that each version has a linux-24.04-x64 build.

findings.title: Workflow had no permissions block and used tag-pinned actions
findings.evidence: No `permissions:` key; actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-python@v5 are moving tags.
findings.disposition: Fixed: `permissions: contents: read` and commit pins resolved from the GitHub API (checkout v4.4.0 -> 11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262, setup-python v5.6.0 -> a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065; both verified 200).

findings.title: Evidence validator dependencies were undocumented
findings.evidence: The script needs pyyaml and jsonschema plus downloaded schema files, unlike the stdlib-only checker, and is not wired into CI.
findings.disposition: Fixed: the docstring now states the dependencies, the schema sources and the drift risk.

findings.title: Release-prep commit bundles four concerns
findings.evidence: One commit carries the pending readme edits, the four blocker fixes, same-class typo fixes and review evidence, while CONTRIBUTING asks for one concern per PR.
findings.disposition: Documented under CHANGELOG Notes as a deliberate release-prep consolidation rather than a silent deviation.

findings.title: Reviewer artifact committed verbatim with its typos
findings.disposition: Documented under CHANGELOG Notes as intentional, to keep the review record authentic.

findings.title: The published repository is a separate lineage and still carries the original defects
findings.evidence: git merge-base HEAD FETCH_HEAD is empty. The remote main tree still has .gitthub/ (no .github/), .md issue templates, a dummy CITATION.cff with an <owner> placeholder, and the pre-rename name rnd-workflow-team.
findings.why_it_matters: Fixing the defects in this checkout does not fix the live repository. A plain push cannot fast-forward; publishing requires an explicit reconciliation choice (force-push, merge with --allow-unrelated-histories, or re-applying the fixes onto the remote history).
findings.disposition: Open: awaiting the maintainer's reconciliation decision. Nothing was pushed or force-pushed.

findings.title: Published LICENSE is detected as NOASSERTION, not MIT
findings.evidence: GET /repos/e-mudao/rnd-workflow-team-skills and .../license both report license.spdx_id = NOASSERTION, key 'other', for the 1567-byte root LICENSE, while README.md and CITATION.cff claim MIT.
findings.why_it_matters: GitHub shows the repository as 'Other' rather than MIT, so the license claim made to users is not what the platform reports. The local LICENSE has the same structure, so this persists after any push.
findings.disposition: Open: recommended fix is to keep LICENSE verbatim MIT and move the appended 'Scope of this file' paragraph (which also contains the typo 'relavant') into a separate notice or the readme. The cause is a hypothesis; the detection result is observed.

excluded_after_investigation.result: Not a defect. GitHub's form-schema documentation marks `id` Optional (it only feeds URL query prefills).

excluded_after_investigation.suspicion: The Chinese readme's repository tree is misaligned by one column
excluded_after_investigation.result: Not a defect, and my own earlier hand-count was wrong. Measured with a script: both readmes place their descriptions at column 33.

excluded_after_investigation.suspicion: Committed logs embed machine-specific absolute paths
excluded_after_investigation.result: Not machine-identifying: `git grep /Users/` is empty; the matches are the eval harness's own /private/tmp/rnd-team-sync-20261010/work/... scratch paths.

excluded_after_investigation.suspicion: The checker or tests use APIs newer than the CI interpreter
excluded_after_investigation.result: Not observed: 16 .py files parse at feature_version=(3, 11) and (3, 9); no 3.12+ APIs found.

cffconvert.result: Citation metadata are valid according to schema version 1.2.0.

independent_validations.cff_bibtex_render: @misc{..., author = {emudao}, ...} - confirms the family-names semantics noted in F4.

verdict: The four original blockers are genuinely closed. F1 (citation URL) and F2 (no remote) are release-blocking and cannot be closed from inside this checkout; F3-F8 are fixed in the supplemental commit; F9-F10 are documented decisions. Nothing here has been exercised against a real GitHub remote.
remediation_commit_note: These fixes are carried by the single supplemental commit that adds this file. Its SHA is reported in the round's report rather than embedded here, so that the evidence does not have to contain a digest of itself.
